results.controlIntent: Separation of duties is supported by: a. Identifying and documenting [Assignment: organization-defined duties of individuals requiring separation]; and b. Defining system access authorizations to support that separation.

judgment.rationale: AC-5 requires that system access authorizations be defined to support separation of duties. The evidence retrieved shows the endpoint's execution role (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic) is configured with two wildcard policies: (1) s3:* on all resources, and (2) sagemaker:* on all resources. This grants a single role the ability to perform every duty across the ML lifecycle — data ingestion, model training, deployment, endpoint management, and cross-account S3 access — with no functional boundaries enforced. The role name "Generic" further confirms it was not designed around duty-specific access. This configuration directly contradicts AC-5(b), which requires access authorizations to be scoped to support separation of duties. There is no evidence of distinct roles for distinct duties (e.g., a training role vs. an inference role vs. a data-access role), and the overly broad permissions noted in the policy metadata confirm that least-privilege and duty separation principles have not been applied.
gaps: No documentation of identified duties requiring separation (AC-5a) was available through the collector tools — human attestation of any organizational SoD policy documents would be needed to fully assess part (a) of the control.

No evidence of additional roles (e.g., separate training, deployment, or monitoring roles) was retrievable — a broader IAM inventory would clarify whether SoD is enforced at the organizational level even if not at this endpoint's role.

policies.note: Overly broad — training bucket writes and cross-account access not scoped
